t: Find the Occurrence of First Almost Equal Substring
o: Find the leftmost window of length m = |pattern| in s that differs from pattern in at most one position. Brute force compares every window in O(nm) — up to 10^10 for n = 10^5, too slow. The classic trick: a window matches with ≤1 mismatch iff (longest common prefix with pattern) + (longest common suffix with pattern) ≥ m − 1. Both quantities for all windows come from Z-functions of `pattern + '#' + s` and of the reversed strings.
k: Window s[i..i+m-1] is almost equal to pattern iff LCP(pattern, s[i:]) + LCSuffix(pattern, s[i..i+m-1]) ≥ m − 1: the prefix and suffix matches cover all but at most one character.
Z-function on pattern+'#'+s gives every window's LCP with pattern in O(n+m); running it on reversed strings gives the suffix-match lengths.
Exact matches (LCP = m) automatically satisfy the inequality.

a.i: For each starting index, compare characters and count mismatches, stopping early after 2 mismatches.
s: Slide a window of length m over s
Count mismatches per window, aborting at 2
Return the first index with ≤ 1 mismatch
a.t: O(nm) — too slow for n = 10^5 but correct

a.i: z1 = Z(pattern + '#' + s) gives, for each window start i, the LCP a = z1[m+1+i]. z2 = Z(reversed pattern + '#' + reversed s) gives the common-suffix length b of the window ending at i+m-1. The window needs at most one change iff a + b ≥ m − 1.
s: For each i, check z1[m+1+i] + z2[m+1+n-m-i] >= m-1 and return the first such i
a.t: O(n + m) — two linear Z-function computations and one linear scan
a.sp: O(n + m) for the concatenated strings and Z-arrays

w: The prefix+suffix coverage argument is the heart: if a and b overlap or leave a gap of at most one character, one edit suffices; note a + b can exceed m − 1 harmlessly. Common bug: reversing indices when reading z2 (window [i, i+m-1] maps to position n-m-i in the reversed string). Follow-up (k mismatches): the same idea generalizes with suffix automata / Z-arrays per residue class, or polynomial hashing with binary search per mismatch.
